notes:
Account snapshot:
- Mid-market collaboration SaaS (B2B) focused on team knowledge + in-app help.
- Current stack: Postgres + product microservices, all in AWS (us-east-1). Looking to add LLM-powered contextual help and doc search.
- Primary goals: reduce live support load, increase self-serve resolution, fast snippet generation for KB and release notes.

Engagement history / timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-15: Inbound sign-up; quick API trial (hosted) started. AE Maya intro email.
- 2026-01-20: Demo w/ product + infra; highlighted token-level cost dashboard and model catalog.
- 2026-02-01: 4-week Hosted API POC kickoff (goal: embeddings for search + chat for support agent augmentation). POC scope doc: Drive link above.
- 2026-02-18: Mid-POC sync (ff_2026-02-11). Observed: embeddings latency ~45ms median, generation P95 ~320ms, acceptable. Noted higher tail under concurrent load.
- 2026-02-25: Hosted POC wrap call (ff_2026-02-25). Product team: "latency looks good, cost unclear at scale". Requested Dedicated pricing to model 6-12 month economics.
- 2026-03-03: Redwood SE (Daniel) ran throughput profiling with sample traffic patterns; suggested batching + KV cache would reduce token cost by 18-25%.
- 2026-03-05: Internal Lotus Bridge finance ops pinged for committed pricing and ramp schedule.
- 2026-03-08: Pricing/term negotiation call; Redwood provided draft term sheet and three commit options (see pricing bullets below).

POC findings & technical constraints:
- Workload: mixed embeddings (batch upsert), chat augmentation for support flows, short-form summarization for PR notes.
- Latency requirement: conversational flows P95 < 400ms; embeddings batch throughput target 2k vectors/min.
- Throughput expected at launch: 15-30 requests/sec with bursts up to 100 rps during product launches.
- Model preference: open-model variants with Redwood-verified performance; willing to use 7B/13B quantized variants for most flows, want fallback to higher-capacity model during peak for quality-sensitive prompts.
- Deployment: require VPC peering and private egress; KMS integration for key management; SOC2 compliance mandatory; data residency: US-only for customer data.

Pricing / Dedicated packaging discussion (from negotiation call) — key items:
- Commit tiers proposed by Redwood: A) Base: 200k tokens/day committed (3-month ramp), B) Growth: 500k tokens/day (2-month ramp), C) Enterprise: 1.5M tokens/day (immediate commit). Lotus Bridge prefers Growth tier as target.
- Burst: Redwood offered 2x burst above committed at 50% higher unit price; Lotus Bridge requested predictable burst cap (max 3x but soft cap after 2x triggers quota alerts).
- Overage: overage pricing proposed at 1.5x of committed rate; Lotus Bridge asking for quarterly true-up rather than daily billing for overages.
- Ramp schedule: proposed 2-month stepped ramp (40% -> 70% -> 100%) for Growth tier; finance prefers 3-month ramp to align revenue recognition and reduce cash pressure.
- Minimum term / discounts: 12-month term with escalating discount at higher commits; Lotus Bridge pushing for 9-month pilot with option to convert to 12-mo committed.
- Burstable reserve: Redwood suggested paid burst reserve (prepaid credits) as alternative to high overage rates. Lotus Bridge wants clearer math on break-even vs pay-as-you-go.

Security & procurement notes:
- Security engaged: initial questionnaire complete. Next: deeper KMS/HSM architecture call with security team (requested this week).
- Legal: standard Redwood terms acceptable except need specific data residency language + incident response SLA.
- Procurement timeline: Lotus Bridge procurement expects signed terms by 2026-04 to hit product launch window in June.

Open questions / blockers (short):
- Need formalized burst cap and overage cadence (daily vs monthly true-up).
- Legal needs explicit US-only data residency and retention windows.
- Finance wants a 3-month ramp option and clearer monthly ARR impact modeling.

Next steps (action items):
- AE (Maya) to circulate updated term sheet with: 3-month ramp option, burst reserve pricing examples, and monthly vs quarterly true-up scenarios (by 2026-03-11).
- SE (Daniel) to produce a cost projection spreadsheet using Lotus Bridge traffic traces + Redwood batching suggestions (deliver by 2026-03-12).
- Security sync meeting to be scheduled for KMS/HSM + VPC peering (target: 2026-03-10).
- Lotus Bridge procurement to confirm preferred commit tier (Growth 500k tokens/day) and decide between prepaid burst reserve or overage cushion (decision due 2026-03-20).

Stated customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "We liked the hosting performance; need price predictability — spikes kill our unit-economics."
- "If you can guarantee a burst model that doesn't bankrupt us during launches, we can commit to a 12-month contract."

CRM notes style: short, pragmatic, a few typos and shorthand tolerated. Current sentiment: interested but price-sensitive; incline to move to Dedicated if legal and burst mechanics are clarified.
